answer: The cheapest real defence: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because shale only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, bridge is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any prism approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
